body: Would love to see this fixed. Also running into this and it is relevant to my development right now. This is a RayCast3D and a ShapeCast3D with a box shape. As you can see, both of them stop registering collisions once inside the CSG box. Also tested with trimesh StaticBody3Ds, same result. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8185f875-ede6-4d66-9f49-5f2e600b5b53) Note that this works with BoxShape StaticBodies as seen here: I understand that trimeshes are hollow, but I would expect at least ShapeCast3Ds to still work when their shape is overlapping a trimesh wall while the origin is inside.

It has occurred to me that it doesn't work because trimeshes also don't have a backface by default. If you enable `Backface Collision` on the trimesh shape, shapecasts and raycasts do work from inside correctly (as long as they are hitting a wall). This isn't ideal but not sure what could be done about it

Yeah, I noticed this for a while too. To the point that I never trusted shapecast to be reliable. Box3D shape has been fixed in JoltPhysics, but Trimesh/ConcavePolygon3D collisions are still bugged. And since CSG uses ConcavePolygon3D internally, they are too. Here are some examples using 4.6.1 and JoltPhysics (new default physics) _Using a shapecast box and a raycast with hit_inside enable for comparrison. The shapecast is going 0.8 downwards. The top of the shapecast box is where the raycast starts._ **CSG/Trimesh** (left) | **Trimesh with backface collision** (right) Using backface collision **almosts** fixes it. It just has that strange glitch at the end where it goes back up. But even so, that is a workaround because backface collision is more taxing and hopefully should not be required for shapecasts to work properly. --- **BoxShape3D** For comparrison, here is how BoxShape3D works in JoltPhysics. The "Correct" result. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e98c149-6727-4b1b-87c1-c76c637f71a1 --- Unfortunately, **CSG shapes don't allow you to enable backface_collision** for the workaround. But it is very easy to add that option to csg_shapes to at least have the same fix as trimesh collision shapes. I tested it here by hard coding csg to use backface_collision it and indeed it works. But adding an option in the CSGNodes seems easy enough. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/191546b9-aa66-4a06-8a5b-0ca77a77be12 But the strange glitch at the end is concerning. And hopefully it could work without having to add backface_collision, since that wastes performance. Here is the modification at csg_shape.cpp: **Edit:** That strange glitch at the end is the expected behavior. Because I used a box of 0.8 height, going down 0.5 inside a 1.0 floor, it only shapecasts on the bottom side for a very small window, which is what causes this position flicker "glitch".
